### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address-canonical.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address-canonical.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bbc06d90fbd6f4994caa1322a74e62a16b18a047` — the merge of head `aa57f6ddcbd8620bc216cb70f2b618ab5c055c91` into base `870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bbc06d90fbd6f4994caa1322a74e62a16b18a047 && git checkout bbc06d90fbd6f4994caa1322a74e62a16b18a047
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9 aa57f6ddcbd8620bc216cb70f2b618ab5c055c91 && git checkout -B drift-repro 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9 && git merge --no-ff aa57f6ddcbd8620bc216cb70f2b618ab5c055c91

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 870ebce333bf0a5794307febe077ab5652cfbfe9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 「允许的 IP 段」里的 IPv6 网段（如 `2001:db8::/32`）按网段生效：登录闸门放行网段内的 IPv6 用户，设置保存检查也认得出保存者在网段内；精确 IPv6 地址按值匹配，不论写法。
- **为什么改：** 原匹配只认 IPv4 网段，IPv6 网段被当文字比对永不匹配，网段内的 IPv6 用户登录和保存全被拒（#30320，#30309 的跟进项）。
- **风险与回滚：** 只放宽到设置本来承诺的语义；地址族互不放行，写错的 IPv6 前缀只匹配基地址；IPv4 条目读法不变。回滚即撤本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` 的 `ipMatchesRange` / `readMatchedAddress`。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts src/auth-manager.test.ts`。
- **需要您做的：** 无，席位经合并队列落地（非受管面，189 行）。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT。声明面复审由席位在 `TIER_DEFAULT` 完成（见下），PASS。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#2 · head `aa57f6ddcbd8620bc216cb70f2b618ab5c055c91`

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT` (declaration face: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no `packages/spec/**` and no governed path). Implemented-by `session_01Utp6CXwcgsAkqebfzjnfiS`; Reviewed-by `session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL`.

- **形态:** draft, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`), no assignee, no review request; 5 files, +160 −29; `check-governed-merges --pr 30392`: NOT governed (0 of 5 paths), 189 lines ≤ 3000. Commits: red pin `d66430431b` → fix `d9855b3c6d` → merge of `main` `fdad1786` (`aa57f6dd`).
- **Diff read (seat):** `ipMatchesRange` reads both sides through `readMatchedAddress` (IPv4 → uint32 via `ipv4ToInt`; otherwise `parseIpv6Literal`, already in the file, after dropping a `%zone`; `::ffff:0:0/96` dotted or hex folds to IPv4). An IPv4 base keeps the earlier prefix reading and its exact-base fallback; an IPv6 base takes a 1–3 digit prefix ≤ 128, otherwise `/128` (base only); families never cross; `::/0` loops zero groups and matches every pure IPv6 address. Unreadable text on either side falls back to a trimmed text comparison, as before. Every former IPv4 and mapped-dotted case reads the same (checked: no-slash IPv4, out-of-range IPv4 prefix, mapped base with an IPv4 prefix). The two doors (`isClientIpAllowed`, `allowed-ip-ranges.ts`) still call the one function. `client-address-canonical.ts` changes a comment only.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no` holds: no export, error code, settings key or manifest shape moves; the change admits clients an entry already names, which is the setting's documented CIDR meaning. `Metadata-protocol: none`; changeset `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, the same two lines in the PR body and the changeset; no `Skills-docs:` line owed.
- **Pins:** unit tests for IPv6 prefix, by-value exact match, family separation and malformed IPv6 prefixes; both doors driven through the real settings route and the sign-in gate in `allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts`. Dev: 6 red on the unfixed tree, 4 ablations red then restored; plugin-auth 3925 passed; derived gates 62/62; lint 0.
- **门禁 check-runs:** 14 success, 13 skipped, 18 in progress, 0 failed at ACCEPT; auto-merge waits on the required contexts.
- **落地条款:** Fixes #30320. Ordinary queue landing by this seat: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` on this head. PR #30376 and PR #30365 edit other files or other hunks of `plugin-auth`; the queue rebuilds on each merge.
